pdf_row.text: Union retreat order Jul 1 | 15:45; 16:00; 16:30; 17:00 | 16:00 | other three

basis.text: Two reports of the officers who gave the orders, in the Official Records: Wadsworth (4 Jul 1863, p. 266) 'at 3.45 o'clock I ordered the command to retire'; Howard (31 Aug 1863, p. 704) 'At 4.10 p. m. ... I sent a positive order to the commanders of the First and Eleventh Corps to fall back'. They are two orders at two levels, ten-odd minutes of clock apart; 'about 4' is Howard's conditional word and the enemy's advance; 'nearly 5' is Robinson's receipt of the order; 4.30 dates a regiment's fall-back and the columns' arrival on Cemetery Hill.

default.label: 15:45 to 16:10: Wadsworth ordered the First Division back at 3.45; Howard ordered both corps back at 4.10
default.basis_text: The two ends are two orders with clock readings, both by the officer who gave them: Wadsworth for his division (3.45, report of 4 Jul 1863) and Howard for the First and Eleventh Corps (4.10, report of 31 Aug 1863). Everything else the plan lists is the same retreat seen at another moment: Howard's conditional word about 4, the enemy's advance about 4, a regiment's fall-back at about 4.30 and Robinson's receipt nearly 5. No clock correction is applied.

animation.note: The first retirement is drawn at 15:45, the earliest order with a clock reading (Wadsworth's division, which was the right of the First Corps); the corps-wide order of 16:10 and the later hours stay selectable. This is an order, not an arrival: the printed arrival on Cemetery Hill stays as the gates have it.

default.note: The retreat was not one order: it was ordered at two levels within about twenty-five minutes and received last by Robinson's division. A single instant would hide that.

positions.label: 15:45: Wadsworth orders the First Division to retire (his report of 4 Jul 1863)

support.quote: at 3.45 o'clock I ordered the command to retire

witness.name: James S. Wadsworth
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding First Division, First Corps; on McPherson and Seminary Ridges

support.note: Wadsworth's report of 4 July 1863 (Doubleday's report, p. 251, prints the same sentence as Wadsworth's): after Schurz fell back about 2.30 and he was 'outflanked on both right and left, heavily pressed in front', 'at 3.45 o'clock I ordered the command to retire'. Order given by the writer for his own division.

support.quote: On the morning of July 1, at 8 a. m., the division moved from Marsh Creek on Gettysburg

witness.name: James S. Wadsworth
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding First Division, First Corps; on McPherson and Seminary Ridges

support.note: context: states the day only, not the hour; exact is set for the day the value needs. Dates the day of the 3.45 sentence: the same report, the opening of its account of 1 July.

positions.label: About 16:00: Howard's word to Doubleday to fall back if he must; Doubleday's enemy advance 'about 4 p. m.'

support.quote: About 4 p. m. I sent word to General Doubleday that, if he could not hold out longer, he must fall back, fighting, to Cemetery Hill

witness.name: Oliver O. Howard
witness.role: Major General, commanding Eleventh Corps and, after Reynolds fell, the field

support.note: Howard's report: about 4 p.m. he sent word to Doubleday that if he could not hold out longer he must fall back to Cemetery Hill: a conditional word, ten minutes before the 'positive order' at 4.10.

support.quote: About 4 p. m. the enemy, having been strongly re-enforced

witness.name: Abner Doubleday
witness.role: Major General, commanding the First Corps

support.note: Doubleday's report (14 Dec 1863): about 4 p.m. the enemy advanced in force; 'It became necessary to retreat'; this dates the enemy's advance, not his order.

support.quote: I now gave orders to fall back, this and Meredith's brigades covering the movement

witness.name: Abner Doubleday
witness.role: Major General, commanding the First Corps

support.note: Doubleday's own order to fall back, given after the advance 'about 4 p. m.': no clock reading of its own. He adds that the division commanders' statements 'are slightly conflicting'.

inference.step: Howard's 'About 4 p. m.' word to Doubleday permits a fall-back but is conditional; Doubleday's 'About 4 p. m.' dates the enemy's advance and his order followed it with no clock reading. Both place a fall-back order about 16:00, not at a stated minute.

reason_not_chosen.text: Howard's 4 p.m. word to Doubleday is conditional and Doubleday gives no hour for his own order; the orders with a clock reading are Wadsworth's 3.45 and Howard's 4.10.

positions.label: About 16:30: a regiment ordered back at the seminary (McFarland); columns reach Cemetery Hill (Howard)

support.quote: I ordered the shattered remnants of as brave a regiment as ever entered the field to fall back [...] At this instant, 4.30 p. m., I was hit by a flank fire in both legs

witness.name: George F. McFarland
witness.role: Lieutenant Colonel, 151st Pennsylvania (Biddle's brigade); wounded at the seminary

support.note: McFarland's report (Juniata County, Pa., 15 Mar 1864, written from his recovery): he ordered the remnant of his regiment back and was hit 'at this instant, 4.30 p. m.' about 20 paces from the seminary: a regimental fall-back order at about 16:30.

support.quote: At 4.30 p. m. the columns reached Cemetery Hill, the enemy pressing hard

witness.name: Oliver O. Howard
witness.role: Major General, commanding Eleventh Corps and, after Reynolds fell, the field

support.note: Howard's report: the retiring columns reached Cemetery Hill at 4.30: the retreat was then in progress; this dates arrival on the hill, not an order.

inference.step: McFarland's 4.30 is the minute he was hit, just after he ordered his regiment back; Howard's 4.30 is the arrival of the columns on Cemetery Hill. Neither is a general order; a regiment's fall-back order fell about 16:25 to 16:30, and the retiring columns were on the hill at 4.30.

reason_not_chosen.text: No report gives a general order at 4.30. The hour dates a regiment's fall-back at the seminary and the columns' arrival on Cemetery Hill, both after the orders of 3.45 and 4.10.

positions.label: About 17:00: Robinson's division receives its order to withdraw, 'nearly 5 p. m.' (his report)

support.quote: from about noon until nearly 5 p. m., when I received orders to withdraw. These orders not being received until all other troops (except Stewart's battery) had commenced moving to the rear

witness.name: John C. Robinson
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding Second Division, First Corps, on the right near the Mummasburg road

support.note: Robinson's report (headed 'Jvly 18, 1863'; the OCR prints the month oddly): his division got its order 'nearly 5 p. m.', after 'all other troops (except Stewart's battery) had commenced moving to the rear'. It dates the receipt of the order by the last division, not the giving of the order.

support.quote: On the morning of Wednesday, the 1st, the division marched from Emmitsburg

witness.name: John C. Robinson
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding Second Division, First Corps

support.note: context: states the day only, not the hour; exact is set for the day the value needs. Dates the day of the 'nearly 5 p. m.' sentence: the same report, headed 'Hdqrs. Second Division, First Army Corps, July 18, 1863'.

reason_not_chosen.text: Robinson says his division received its order after all other troops had begun to move; 'nearly 5 p. m.' is the last order to reach the field, not the retreat order.

weighing.summary: The reports name two orders with clock readings, each given by the writer: Wadsworth's order to his division at 3.45 (written 4 Jul 1863) and Howard's positive order to both corps at 4.10 (written 31 Aug 1863). Everything else in the plan is the same retreat at another moment: 'about 4 p. m.' is Howard's conditional word to Doubleday (ten minutes before the positive order) and the enemy's advance in Doubleday's report, which then 'gave orders to fall back' with no clock reading; 'nearly 5 p. m.' is when Robinson's division received its order after all other troops had begun to move; 4.30 is the minute a regimental commander was hit just after ordering his men back, and the minute Howard puts the columns on Cemetery Hill. No report gives a general order at 4.30. The first delegated pass found these as 'different orders' but kept one hour inside a wide window; the window of this resolution is the span of the two orders themselves. Robinson's 'nearly 5' and Howard's 4.30 cannot both be exact clock readings of the same movement; 'nearly 5' is a round figure and the clocks of the two corps are not shown to agree, so the receipt hour is kept as a separate, unreconciled value and does not enter the window. Weighted, not settled: nothing says which order the picture should follow, only that both are documented.
weighing.who: Wadsworth commanded the First Division and gave its order; Howard commanded the field and gave the order to both corps; Doubleday commanded the First Corps; Robinson commanded the Second Division and received his order late; McFarland commanded the 151st Pennsylvania.
weighing.when: Wadsworth wrote on 4 Jul 1863 (three days, rank 5); Howard on 31 Aug 1863 (61 days, rank 4); Doubleday on 14 Dec 1863; McFarland on 15 Mar 1864; Robinson on 18 Jul 1863 (the date in his heading). Doubleday prints Wadsworth's sentence as 'General Wadsworth says' (p. 251): the same words, one line.
weighing.where: Wadsworth was on the ridge west of the seminary; Howard on Cemetery Hill (he sent aides); Doubleday at the seminary, superintending the final movement; Robinson on the right near the Mummasburg road; McFarland near the seminary.
weighing.how_knew: Wadsworth and Howard each gave their own orders; Doubleday his own; Robinson received his; McFarland gave his regiment's.
weighing.clock: All the Union writers use the Union clock. The plan's note that the two armies' clocks reportedly differed by about 20 minutes is not applied; an Eleventh Corps clock and a First Corps clock might differ by minutes, which could explain a quarter-hour between 3.45 and 4.10 but is not shown.
weighing.independence: Wadsworth's 3.45 is one line (Doubleday prints it as Wadsworth's); Howard's 4.10 and his about-4 word are one writer's report, and the same text is reprinted in Battles and Leaders; the two default orders are separate lines. Each default order has a single non-lead source and is flagged single-source.

source_panel_text: About 15:45 to 16:10 on Jul 1: Wadsworth's report has him ordering his division back at 3.45; Howard's report has his positive order to both corps at 4.10. 'About 4' is Howard's conditional word, 'nearly 5' is when Robinson's division received its order, and 4.30 dates a regiment's fall-back. Five other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: 16:00 is not an order with a clock reading: 'about 4' is Howard's conditional word and the enemy's advance. The orders are 3.45 (Wadsworth) and 4.10 (Howard); 16:00 stays selectable, labelled inferred.

first_delegated.note: The first pass named the different orders but kept one hour (16:00) inside a window from 15:45 to 17:00, whose late end is Robinson's receipt of an order, not an order. The window of this resolution ends at Howard's 4.10; 16:30 is not 'secondary only': a regiment's fall-back and the columns' arrival fall then.
